messages:
elaine: Quick copy pass request — trying to tighten the landing page for the upcoming launch. Goal: one hero that reads clearly for both Hosted API users and teams who need Dedicated/Private. Can we do mode-agnostic language that still routes folks to the right trial funnels?

mohit: love this. top priorities: clarity on value props, CTA for ‘Try hosted’ vs ‘Contact for Dedicated/Private’, and a short webinar hook.

julia: agree. low friction hero + secondary line for differentiation. something like: 

  Variant A headline: "Production-grade LLM inference: predictable latency, lower unit cost"
  Subhead: "Run with our Hosted API or scale to Dedicated and Private deployments — same API, better economics."

sam: Variant A is good but a bit generic. can we surface a core metric? e.g., "<20ms p99 for real-time apps" — only if we have the benchmark to back it.

elaine: we have internal benchmarks for a few models, not across the whole catalog. prefer to keep metric-free unless we link to a benchmark page. instead: 

  Variant B headline: "Ship LLM features with predictable latency and costs"
  Subhead options: 
  - "Hosted for fast-launch, Dedicated for predictable throughput, Private for regulated workloads."
  - "Same API across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private — pick the mode that fits your SLOs."

tessa: I like Variant B + a quick explainer CTA row below hero: 3 pills: Hosted | Dedicated | Private with 1-line benefit each. That lets business teams jump.

mohit: for inbound routing, propose this mapping: 

  - Clicks on Hosted pill -> UTM: ?utm=hero_mode&utm_mode=hosted -> auto-assign lead to Growth SDR queue
  - Clicks on Dedicated or Private -> route to Enterprise lead form w/ dropdown for infra details -> AE/SE follow-up

copybot: Suggest copy for pills: 
  Hosted — "Start instantly with a hosted API & free credits"
  Dedicated — "Reserved GPU capacity and SLA-backed latency"
  Private — "VPC/on-prem for regulated data + KMS integrations"

julia: these pill lines are great. add a small link under hero: "See benchmarks & models -> /benchmarks" for teams wanting numbers.

sam: webinar hook: 30-40 min technical session + 15 min Q&A. Title draft: "Serving LLMs in Production: latency, cost, and fallbacks". Panel: infra lead + research eng + solutions SE.

elaine: perfect. need copy for the webinar promo (social + landing). Short social post: 

  "How do you keep LLM features fast and affordable? Join our engineers for a live playbook on latency, batching, and routing. Wed May 6 — register: <shortlink>"

mohit: for the landing blurb: 
  "Join Redwood engineers to see real-world benchmarks, routing strategies for graceful degradation, and best practices for development-to-production rollouts. Includes live Q&A."

tessa: inbound lead form fields for Dedicated/Private: company size, expected qps, cloud provider, compliance needs. add checkbox: "I want a capacity planning call". That triggers AE routing.

elaine: we should also prepare a mini benchmark narrative to place under hero: 2–3 bullet highlights. Example: 

  - "Smart KV-caching reduced token costs by ~30% on chat workloads."
  - "Automatic batching kept p95 latency within SLOs while improving throughput."

sam: careful with exact percentages — rephrase: "Caching and smart batching reduced per-token cost in customer workloads and improved throughput while preserving latency SLOs."

julia: placement suggestion: hero -> pill row -> 3 bullets (benchmarks summary) -> CTA row (Try hosted / Contact enterprise) -> webinar CTA small link.

mohit: tracking params for pills & CTAs (copy for devs): 

  Try hosted: /signup?utm_campaign=mode_hero&utm_mode=hosted
  Contact enterprise: /contact?utm_campaign=mode_hero&utm_mode=enterprise
  Webinar register: /events/serve-llms?utm_campaign=webinar_mode_hero

elaine: next steps: copy sprint tomorrow 10am PT to finalize hero, pill copy, and webinar blurb. can someone prep the A/B variants in Figma?

julia: I'll prep the Figma frames (+ a small mobile-first variant).

tessa: I'll draft the enterprise form fields and AE routing rules in the doc.

sam: I'll pull the benchmark sentences we can use (approved language only).

mohit: i'll wire up the UTMs and test the inbound routing after copy lands.

elaine: awesome — thanks all. small ask: can we keep the hero concise (≤12 words) and avoid listing all modes in the headline? use subhead for details.

copybot: scheduled reminder: "Copy sprint — mode-agnostic hero" tomorrow 10:00 PT. :bell: 

elaine: thanks — see you tomorrow. :thumbsup:
